Architecture

How XERJ works: one binary, one node

XERJ is a single Rust binary that is both a search node and its own clients. Run bare, it is the node: an Elasticsearch-compatible REST API on :9200, a native API on :8080, a write-ahead log and immutable segments on local disk. Run with a subcommand, it is a client of a node: autoindex and search for your files, mcp for agents over stdio, and ask for Corpus Hub packs, which starts a node of its own when none answers. There is no JVM and no sidecar. It runs on one machine, and there is no replication between nodes.

Components

What is inside the binary

Nodexerj with no subcommand. The Elasticsearch-compatible API listens on :9200 (indices, bulk, search, aggregations, kNN, scroll), the native API on :8080. Both bind 127.0.0.1 unless told otherwise. ES-compat API · native API
StorageOne append-only WAL per index and a list of immutable segments, each three files (columnar data, skip index, doc-id sidecar), all memory-mapped. The default wal_sync = "batched" survives a process crash and can lose up to about 100 ms of acknowledged writes on power loss; "sync" makes every write power-loss durable. Storage & WAL
EmbedderBuilt in and lexical by default: feature hashing over words and sub-words, offline, not a neural model. --embed-mode neural downloads about 90 MB once; an OpenAI-compatible endpoint can be configured instead. Vectors & kNN
autoindex · search · defClients of a running node. autoindex sniffs each file by content, writes explicit mappings and streams documents with idempotent ids; it is CLI-only and must run where the files are. Zero-config autoindex
ask · hubThe Corpus Hub client. It verifies the signed catalogue, routes the question locally, pulls one pre-indexed pack from GitHub Releases into a node (yours on :9200, or one it starts from :9300 up), and keeps packs under a 4 GB budget. xerj ask
mcpA Model Context Protocol server on stdio with 17 tools. It opens no port and proxies to the node in XERJ_URL. CLI · mcp
Raft ringOptional cluster mode with leader election and authenticated transport. Nothing in the write path rides on it yet: indices and documents stay node-local (#1170). Clustering

Request paths

Two paths through it

xerj "question"
  1. Load the cached catalogue, or fetch it from hub.xerj.org; check its ed25519 signature.
  2. Pick one corpus from the per-corpus term sketches and the project's lockfiles.
  3. Find a node on XERJ_URL or :9200, or start one from :9300 up.
  4. If the pack is not local, download it from GitHub Releases, verify signature and SHA-256, restore it.
  5. Query the pack's indices and print hits with file:line, pin and licence.
xerj autoindex <folder>
  1. Walk the folder, skipping the built-in ignore list, and sniff each file by its bytes.
  2. Infer field types and date encodings; PUT explicit mappings for ax-* indices.
  3. Stream documents into the node with idempotent ids; resumable after kill -9.
  4. Write what it learned to autoindex-catalog, which agents query to orient.
  5. Search with xerj search, the MCP tools, or any Elasticsearch client.

Deploying

Where it runs

  • Targets. Linux (static musl and glibc builds, plus .deb packages), macOS and Windows, each on x86_64 and arm64. The rc.97 Linux x86_64 musl download is about 32 MB; the unpacked binary is about 140 MB.
  • A laptop or a server. The same binary. For a long-running node, the operations guide has a systemd unit, readiness probe and log levels; backup & restore covers the data directory.
  • Offline. The air-gapped recipe stages a release and an optional model on a connected machine.
  • Not a cluster. No replication, shard routing or failover. Size one node for the workload, or use Elasticsearch or OpenSearch where you need a replicated cluster.
  • Memory grows with documents indexed. The server keeps per-segment caches until a merge retires the segment (#1032); index very large corpora one at a time and watch RSS.

Read the source

The engine crates live under engine/crates/. Measurements against Elasticsearch are on benchmarks; the security defaults are on security.
